🛡️ GDPR Compliance

Built-in Art. 30 inspection, Art. 15/20 subject-data export, personal-data field tagging, and configurable retention — all in the engine, no external tooling required.

Overview

BLite 5.0.0 ships a dedicated GDPR subsystem under the BLite.Core.GDPR namespace. It provides:

  • Personal data field tagging — [PersonalData] attribute marks sensitive properties on mapped types.
  • GDPR inspection report — enumerate all collections with their personal-data fields, retention policy, encryption status, and audit status in one call.
  • Subject data export — extract all documents matching a field/value pair across collections and emit a portable JSON report (Art. 15/20).
  • GdprMode.Strict — optional engine mode that rejects schema-less writes to collections that declare a typed schema with personal data.

Marking Personal Data

Decorate properties on your mapped types with [PersonalData] and optionally [DataSensitivity]:

using BLite.Core.GDPR;

public class User
{
    public ObjectId Id { get; set; }
    public string   Name  { get; set; } = "";

    [PersonalData]
    public string Email { get; set; } = "";

    [PersonalData, DataSensitivity(SensitivityLevel.High)]
    public string? PhoneNumber { get; set; }
}

The engine reads these attributes at collection registration time and records the field names in its metadata store — no runtime overhead on the hot path.

Art. 30 — Inspection Report

Generate a complete processing record for one database:

using BLite.Core.GDPR;

var report = GdprEngineExtensions.InspectDatabase(engine);

Console.WriteLine($"Encrypted: {report.IsEncrypted}");
Console.WriteLine($"Audit enabled: {report.IsAuditEnabled}");

foreach (var col in report.Collections)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Collection: {col.Name}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  Personal fields: {string.Join(", ", col.PersonalDataFields)}");
    Console.WriteLine($"  Retention: {col.RetentionPolicy?.MaxAge}");
}

Via BLite.Server REST: GET /api/v1/{dbId}/gdpr/inspect (requires Admin permission).

Art. 15/20 — Subject Data Export

Export all documents for a specific data subject across all collections:

var query = new SubjectQuery
{
    FieldName  = "Email",
    FieldValue = BsonValue.FromString("alice@example.com"),
    Format     = SubjectExportFormat.Json
};

await using var report = await GdprEngineExtensions.ExportSubjectDataAsync(engine, query);
await report.ExportAsJsonAsync(File.OpenWrite("alice-export.json"));

To scope the search to specific collections, set SubjectQuery.Collections:

Collections = ["users", "orders"]

Via BLite.Server REST: POST /api/v1/{dbId}/{collection}/gdpr/export-subject with body {"fieldName":"email","fieldValue":"alice@example.com"}.

Retention Policies

BLite 5.0.0 generalises retention — it is no longer limited to TimeSeries collections. Any typed collection can declare a retention policy:

var col = engine.GetOrCreateCollection<ObjectId, AuditEntry>(mapper);

col.HasRetentionPolicy(new RetentionPolicy
{
    MaxAge           = TimeSpan.FromDays(90),   // delete docs older than 90 days
    TimestampField   = "CreatedAt"
});

// Force an immediate prune (otherwise runs automatically on insert)
await col.PruneAsync();

Secure Erase

When HasSecureErase is configured on a collection, BLite zero-overwrites the page regions previously occupied by a deleted document before reclaiming them. This prevents data recovery from the raw file:

col.HasSecureErase();
Secure erase adds one extra write per deleted document. Enable it only for collections that store personal or sensitive data.

GdprMode.Strict

In strict mode the engine rejects schema-less (dynamic) writes to any collection that has a registered typed schema containing [PersonalData] fields. This prevents accidental untagged writes:

var options = new BLiteEngineOptions
{
    DatabasePath = "mydb.blite",
    GdprMode     = GdprMode.Strict
};

BLite Studio GDPR Page

BLite.Server 2.0.0 adds a dedicated GDPR page at /gdpr in the Blazor Studio that provides:

  • Art. 30 inspection report with encryption badge, audit badge, per-collection personal data fields, and retention summary.
  • Subject data export form — enter field name + value and download a JSON file directly from the browser.
  • One-click Vacuum to compact the database and reclaim free space.
